definition: Channel sales reaches customers through partners such as distributors, resellers, and retailers rather than only through direct sales.
example: A software vendor trains an authorized reseller to sell and support its product.

definition: Character art develops the visual appearance of fictional characters through drawings, paintings, or digital models.
example: A game artist draws several silhouettes before modeling the selected character.

definition: Chart.js is a JavaScript library for rendering common data chart types using the browser’s canvas element.
example: A developer adds a chart that shows week-by-week traffic in an analytics app.

definition: Chip design specifies and verifies the electronic circuits and layout to be fabricated in an integrated circuit.
example: An engineer checks a proposed hardware block for timing and functional correctness before fabrication.

definition: Chipmunk2D is a physics library for simulating rigid bodies, collisions, and constraints in two dimensions.
example: A game developer models a ball bouncing between moving platforms.

definition: Chordiant was an enterprise software platform for customer relationship management and rules-based customer interactions.
example: A service provider maintains a legacy workflow that guides support agents through account inquiries.

definition: Choreography composes and organizes movement in time and space for a performance.
example: A choreographer arranges the dancers’ entrances, spacing, and shared movements.

definition: Chromatography software controls compatible instruments or processes and reports chromatographic measurement data.
example: A quality analyst reviews a chromatogram and checks how the software integrated its peaks.

definition: A chronometer is a precision timekeeping instrument, traditionally associated with navigation or certified accuracy.
example: A maritime exhibit explains how a reliable chronometer let navigators compare local time with reference time.
sense_note: In some occupational lists the term is used more broadly for a precision timer.

definition: Cisco Intersight is an infrastructure management platform for monitoring and operating supported systems from a shared control interface.
example: An infrastructure team reviews firmware compliance for enrolled systems.

definition: Cisco UCS Director automates configuration and operations across supported computing, networking, and storage infrastructure.
example: An administrator uses a predefined workflow to provision a standard development environment.

definition: Civil engineering design develops and verifies plans for infrastructure and built works against conditions, safety requirements, and user needs.
example: An engineer sizes site drainage structures for the design’s expected runoff.

definition: CKEditor is a web-based rich text editor component for authoring and formatting content in applications.
example: A publisher embeds CKEditor in a form that lets editors add links and headings.

definition: Claim processing receives, validates, evaluates, and resolves requests for payment or coverage under applicable rules.
example: An insurance processor compares a submitted claim with the policy and requests missing documents.

definition: Claims modeling uses statistical or computational methods to estimate claim frequency, cost, development, or related outcomes.
example: An insurer models the expected annual cost of reported property claims.
sense_note: This assumes the actuarial or insurance sense; it is not about constructing an argument.

definition: Clarizen was a cloud project and portfolio management platform for coordinating work, schedules, resources, and project reporting.
example: A project lead checks milestones across a program and updates a resource plan.

definition: Clash detection identifies incompatible intersections or clearances between components in a coordinated design model.
example: A construction coordinator finds a duct that overlaps a structural beam before installation.

definition: A classification and regression tree recursively splits observations by predictor values and assigns a class or numerical prediction to each final region.
example: An analyst grows a tree to predict relative order-processing time from workload and staffing.

definition: The U.S. Clean Air Act establishes a federal framework for controlling air pollution, including air quality and emissions standards.
example: An environmental specialist identifies which air-pollution requirements are relevant to an industrial facility.
sense_note: The generic name can refer to other countries’ statutes; this definition assumes the U.S. law.

definition: The U.S. Clean Water Act establishes a federal framework for protecting water quality and regulating certain discharges of pollutants into waters.
example: A facility reviews whether a wastewater discharge needs a permit.
sense_note: This definition assumes the U.S. statute.

definition: ClearDB was a managed cloud database service centered on MySQL-compatible databases.
example: A developer connects an application to an existing hosted ClearDB database.

definition: Client confidentiality protects information learned through a client relationship from disclosure without appropriate authority.
example: A consultant limits circulation of a client’s records to the approved project team.

definition: A clinical data repository stores and organizes patient-related data from clinical systems for authorized retrieval or analysis.
example: A hospital makes laboratory results from several departments available through a shared record.

definition: Clinical documentation improvement clarifies and completes clinical records so they accurately support patient care, coding, and reporting.
example: A specialist asks a clinician to clarify conflicting descriptions of a diagnosis without suggesting an unsupported answer.

definition: Clinical laboratory phlebotomy is the collection and documentation of blood specimens for laboratory analysis.
example: A trained phlebotomist checks patient and specimen identifiers before transferring the sample to the laboratory.

definition: A closed-circuit television camera sends video to a limited monitoring or recording system rather than to a public broadcast.
example: A facility uses an authorized camera to monitor access to a stockroom.

definition: A cloud access security broker applies an organization’s security policies to its use of cloud applications or services.
example: A security team monitors whether approved cloud applications are being used to store restricted information.

definition: Cloud-native development builds software to use cloud delivery, operational automation, and independently manageable infrastructure or components.
example: A team automates deployment and scaling for a service across multiple instances.

definition: CNC programming specifies the controlled motions and instructions a computer numerical control machine uses to manufacture a part.
example: A machinist simulates a toolpath before running it on a milling machine.

definition: Cocoa Touch is Apple’s application framework layer for building touch-oriented applications on iOS and related platforms.
example: A developer uses UIKit views and controllers to build a touch-based interface.

definition: CocoaPods is a dependency manager that integrates libraries into projects built with Xcode.
example: A maintainer refreshes a project’s prescribed dependency versions and rebuilds it.

definition: CocoonJS was a platform for packaging and running HTML5 applications and games as mobile apps.
example: A maintainer reviews how a legacy web game accesses native device features.
sense_note: This is distinct from Apache Cocoon.

definition: Collaboration software helps people exchange information, coordinate work, or jointly edit shared materials.
example: Several reviewers comment on a proposal and track decisions in a shared workspace.

definition: Collaboration is working with others toward a shared outcome by coordinating contributions, decisions, and responsibilities.
example: Designers and engineers jointly resolve an accessibility problem before release.

definition: Collaborative Planning, Forecasting and Replenishment is a supply-chain practice in which trading partners share plans and demand forecasts to coordinate inventory replenishment.
example: A retailer and supplier exchange demand projections ahead of a seasonal promotion.

definition: Color matching adjusts or selects colors so a sample or output visually or instrumentally agrees with a target under specified conditions.
example: A print technician compares a proof to a reference under controlled lighting.

definition: Color, material and finish design specifies the visible and tactile surface qualities of a product to achieve intended practical and aesthetic effects.
example: A designer chooses a textured finish that reduces visible fingerprints while supporting the product’s palette.

definition: A combine harvester cuts a crop, threshes it, and separates the usable grain in one machine.
example: An operator harvests wheat and monitors how much grain is lost behind the machine.

definition: Commercial loan documentation records a business borrower’s obligations and the terms, conditions, and security interests associated with a loan.
example: A loan officer assembles the signed agreement and collateral records for review.

definition: Commissioning, qualification and validation are coordinated activities for putting a system into service, verifying specified operation, and documenting consistent fitness for intended use.
example: An equipment team tests a newly installed line against requirements before documenting its authorized production use.
